subject: Operator-license vs Platform-fee: scenario comparison & invoicing path
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medisys.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
Cc: Alice Chen <alice.chen@medisys.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: cost scenarios for private deployment (operator license vs platform fee)

Hi Priya —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement asked me to pull together two high-level commercial scenarios so we can compare cashflow and exit risk before we move to legal:

Option A (Operator-license heavy):
- Operator license per active node (site-level). Lower monthly platform fee (20% of list).
- Upfront seat/operator purchase for pilot (12 months) then true-up quarterly.
- Pros: clear per-node economics, easier to attribute cost to sites.
- Cons: higher initial capex, unclear handling of node reallocation across sites.

Option B (Platform-fee heavy):
- Larger annual platform fee amortized monthly; fewer operator licenses included.
- Pros: predictable OPEX, simpler billing.
- Cons: higher sunk platform fee if we exit early.

Key asks from our CFO/procurement:
1) Can you show a 24-month P&L for both options with a pilot-to-scale scenario (pilot: 3 sites, scale: 20 sites)?
2) What are the invoice cadence options (monthly, net30, milestone)?
3) For Option A, can operator licenses be re-assigned if we decommission nodes?
4) Any standard SOW / sample invoice you can provide for our Legal and Finance teams.

We'd like a one-page comparison and a recommended approach (our execs want a clear recommendation). Can you get something to me by EOD next Tuesday (Nov 30)?

Thanks —
Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure Procurement
Medisys Health

From: Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@medisys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: cost scenarios for private deployment (operator license vs platform fee)

Sanjay —

Appreciate the clear asks. I've pulled together a compact scenario comparison and recommendation (attached: PrivDeploy_Scenario_Comparison_Medisys.xlsx). High-level summary below — see the spreadsheet for the 24-month P&L and assumptions.

Executive summary (recommendation):
- Recommend a hybrid onramp: pilot on Operator-license heavy model for the first 12 months (3 pilot sites) to minimize initial platform commitment and let engineering validate KV-cache/batching footprint. After pilot, transition to a blended model: lower incremental operator licenses + a staggered platform fee amortized over 24 months.

Why hybrid?
- Pilot reduces upfront platform exposure and lets us size accurate throughput.
- Transitioning to a blended platform fee after the pilot reduces procurement friction at scale and simplifies cross-site failover licensing.

Numbers (example, see sheet for full breakouts):
- Pilot (3 sites): Option A cash outlay ~ $145k year-1 (operator licenses + small platform fee). Option B ~ $220k year-1.
- At 20 sites scale, Option A annualized TCO ~ $1.1M; Option B ~ $1.05M depending on discounting and amortization windows.

Invoice cadence options we support:
- Monthly invoices (net30), or
- Quarterly invoices with net30 by default, or
- Milestone invoicing tied to SOW acceptance & production cutover (commonly used for large pilots).

Operator-license re-assignment:
- We can support transfer of operator licenses between sites in the same legal entity (subject to notification and a 30-day re-allocation window). We will not credit decommissioned nodes retroactively beyond the current term unless part of an agreed true-up. Language included in the attached SOW draft.

Next steps requested from you:
- Confirm preferred invoice cadence (monthly vs quarterly) and PO lead time.
- Confirm whether Medisys requires tax-exempt handling or special invoicing fields.

I've looped in Marissa (commercial ops) and David (finance) to propose invoice & SOW wording and an example invoice schedule. If you want, we can convert the spreadsheet into an executive one-pager for your CFO.

Attachments: PrivDeploy_Scenario_Comparison_Medisys.xlsx (scenario sheets + assumptions)

Best,
Priya Natarajan

Subject: Re: Request: cost scenarios for private deployment (operator license vs platform fee)

Sanjay / Priya —

Quick finance note after reviewing Priya's sheet. I attached a sample invoice schedule PDF (InvoiceSchedule_Medisys.pdf) that shows three common flows we can support: monthly (net30), quarterly net30 with milestone trigger, and upfront 20% platform fee + monthly amortization.

A few clarifications / options that matter to procurement:
- PO timing: if you issue a PO before Dec 15, we can lock the pilot pricing in for 90 days.
- Taxes: invoices will be net of local sales tax; if you have a resale certificate please share.
- License transfers (operator licenses): we offer a 30-day reassign window with a pro-rata credit toward future purchases for decommissions if you select the hybrid model AND commit to the 24-month blended amortization at scale.

Suggested contract language (short):
- "Operator licenses are issued per active node at time of invoice. Licensing assignment may be transferred within the same legal entity with 30 days' notice; decommissioned nodes are not retroactively credited except as provided in a separate true-up agreement or by mutual written consent."

If procurement prefers a pure OPEX model, we can prepare a 24-month amortization plan with a slightly higher platform fee and vendor-hosted failure credits. Otherwise hybrid is the lowest-risk route.

Attachments: InvoiceSchedule_Medisys.pdf

Thanks —
David Kim
